nodes.label: session.ts / session/patch.ts (pure core)
nodes.rationale: Log is commands plus before/after patches; undo appends the inverse patch.

nodes.label: Item Overrides (filterable, tradable, excluded, quest, unpriceable)
nodes.norm_label: item overrides (filterable, tradable, excluded, quest, unpriceable)

nodes.label: Four-Level Composition (category > subcategory > item > variant)
nodes.rationale: A condition is replaced by condition+operator key, because MapTier >= 11 and MapTier <= 15 are two conditions; null removes an earlier level's condition.

nodes.label: Taxonomy Governing Laws
nodes.rationale: Only droppable items; priced items first with unique conditions; unpriced droppables kept as unpriceable rather than excluded.

nodes.label: listing selector (PoeWatch field match)
nodes.rationale: The fact is authored twice on purpose: GemLevel >= 6 is what the filter asks, gemLevel: 6 is which listing to price off; the catalog copies conditions and never reads them.

nodes.label: Variants (a variant is an item)
nodes.rationale: A price attaches to a variant, not an item; row price and variant prices are exclusive.

nodes.label: Nested rate-limit tiers (search and fetch)
nodes.rationale: Only the 6h tier governs volume; short windows govern burst shape.

nodes.label: Central scheduler with per-IP dual ledgers
nodes.norm_label: central scheduler with per-ip dual ledgers
nodes.rationale: Single process so pacing is centrally accounted; separate search and fetch buckets; LRU IP selection; park IP on 429; persist counters to SQLite; pace to target volume.

nodes.label: Work unit (1 search + 3 fetches)
nodes.rationale: The 1:3 search-to-fetch ratio drives all sizing; units stay atomic on one IP so the two ledgers stay in sync.

nodes.label: 60% utilization planning headroom
nodes.rationale: Tripping the 6h tier costs a long lockout and slow recovery; extra IPs are cheap.

nodes.label: Fetch endpoint is the bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Fetch has the higher limit but is called 3x per unit, capping 333 units per 6h per IP.

nodes.label: Rejected: Fargate Spot per request
nodes.rationale: Fresh random IPs cannot be tracked against a 6h rolling budget.

nodes.label: Taxonomy (items keyed by metadata id)
nodes.rationale: Keyed by metadata id because display names collide (skill gem Wildfire vs unique jewel Wildfire).

nodes.norm_label: condition kinds (boolean, numeric, ordered, strings, enums, sockets, counted, gem)

nodes.label: = partial vs == exact text match
nodes.rationale: Emit == for exact base names or buckets overlap (BaseType "Gold" matches Gold Ring).

nodes.label: writeJsonAtomic (temp file + rename)
nodes.rationale: Readers see whole old or whole new file; S3 has no rename and will need its own answer.

nodes.label: Key layout shared by format, not code
nodes.norm_label: key layout shared by format, not code

nodes.label: @poe/lake
nodes.rationale: Owns how bytes are stored, never where: each app keeps its own key layout as its contract with readers.

nodes.label: latest is a real copy; pin by version
nodes.norm_label: latest is a real copy; pin by version
nodes.rationale: Two calls can straddle a promote, and rows and categories are separate files; read the version off the first answer and pass it from then on.

nodes.label: getCompactData (/compact, all=true)
nodes.rationale: Without all=true PoeWatch omits every crafting base, so the package always sends it.

nodes.label: getGems (Gems.min.json)
nodes.rationale: Keyed by variant id; group by gameId for one entry per gem.

nodes.label: .min variant choice per file
nodes.rationale: Spectres.min.json is published empty and base_items.min.json drops null keys, so only Gems and Essence take .min.

nodes.label: VWAP invariant (volume pair = ratio)
nodes.rationale: VWAP lands inside the ratio band in every checked market: a price band plus a volume-weighted point.

nodes.label: Pruning rare features (MIN threshold)
nodes.rationale: Rare pairs give noisy huge lift and pair counting grows quadratically; use a lower floor for rare namespaces.

nodes.label: Rate-limit header reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Local-only counters drift; treating server-reported state as authoritative makes the limiter self-correcting.

nodes.label: Panel Security Model
nodes.rationale: Renderer is untrusted; approval sends a plan id, not a plan, so a compromised renderer cannot forge training feedback. The .s3 folder itself is trusted.

nodes.label: Duplicated model loaders (tech debt)
nodes.rationale: Loaders copied from apps/admin-panel/run-models cannot sit in lib/ because they read files.

nodes.label: Generate-and-Verify
nodes.rationale: One model proposes, the executor runs it, a separate model checks before the next step.

nodes.label: Router-Worker Pattern
nodes.rationale: A cheap classifier picks the tool, a separate generator fills that one tool's arguments.

nodes.label: getItemData
nodes.rationale: Lists only what players have listed; a new league's uniques are absent until traded, so it is not the game's catalogue.

nodes.label: Exports share no vocabulary

nodes.label: fetchCurrencyHour
nodes.rationale: CDN publishes no limits but shares the IP budget behind Cloudflare, so it is paced by the same limiter.

nodes.label: GGG Rate Limiter (header-driven)
nodes.rationale: GGG answers overruns with timed bans, so one limiter per IP is updated from server headers, holds never shrink, and each rule keeps one slot of headroom.

nodes.label: Required userAgent (contact)
nodes.rationale: GGG asks the user agent name a reachable contact; a default would send one that does not exist.

nodes.label: Hour-keyed Response Cache
nodes.rationale: Entries expire by key rather than by age: the hour is in the key, old files stop being asked for.

nodes.label: Bounded fan-out (concurrency 4)
nodes.rationale: poe.ninja's terms ask callers to be reasonable; first failure abandons the run because half a market is not a market.

nodes.label: itemClass cannot be read
nodes.rationale: Payload does not honour documented rarity meaning; what a row is comes from the requested type via item-types.ts.

nodes.label: A test must fail for a reason TypeScript cannot see
nodes.norm_label: a test must fail for a reason typescript cannot see

nodes.label: Bronze/Silver/Gold Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Bronze is reused on rerun because the hour is gone and refetching gives a different answer; silver and gold rebuild.

nodes.label: Build and Publish Are Separate
nodes.rationale: A build changes nothing anyone else reads; only catalog:publish copies gold into latest/.

nodes.label: Drawable Row Rule
nodes.rationale: Quest rows are out because the game always shows quest items, so pricing them styles nothing.

nodes.label: Authored Rows (authored/<slug>, replaces, reason)
nodes.rationale: reason is required: a hand-written row with no reason records that somebody decided, not what.

nodes.label: Seeded and Manual Files
nodes.rationale: A manual key replaces the seeded list whole; seeds read only RePoE and the taxonomy never touches PoeWatch.

nodes.label: Six Version Files Published as Two
nodes.norm_label: six version files published as two

nodes.label: Taxonomy Validator Refusals
nodes.rationale: tsc never reads .json and a published version is immutable, so both tables are checked before publish.

nodes.label: Verified in game: map influence conditions
nodes.norm_label: verified in game: map influence conditions
nodes.rationale: A map's influence is an implicit, so HasImplicitMod True alone catches influenced maps; originator needs HasInfluence None and CorruptedMods 0.

nodes.label: Do Not Author Class Beside BaseType
nodes.norm_label: do not author class beside basetype
nodes.rationale: BaseType == is exact, and no filterable name needs a class to disambiguate.

nodes.label: Shared key layout (format, not code)
nodes.rationale: App and @poe/taxonomy each build the same key strings; changing one breaks at runtime only.

nodes.label: Taxonomy Versions (draft/publish/promote)
nodes.rationale: The count is the identity and never reused; published versions are immutable; only newest draft publishable; registry is the index because the lake cannot list.

nodes.label: Execution match scoring
nodes.rationale: Two different JSON answers that do the same thing both count.

nodes.label: Scenarios (request, setup, steps)
nodes.rationale: Every scenario is played through the real executeCommand, so no example teaches a plan that cannot run.

nodes.label: buildFilterMatcher
nodes.rationale: Compiles blocks once and indexes by BaseType == names so bulk runs only walk relevant blocks.

nodes.label: FilterItem
nodes.rationale: A missing key fails its condition, negation included; the item parser fills defaults so the evaluator never guesses.

nodes.label: formatNote / formatCondition
nodes.rationale: Write the note rather than build the string so writer and reader cannot drift; fixed key order makes filters comparable as text.

nodes.label: Filter Block Shape
nodes.rationale: Every block must end with exactly one #@ note line; anything else throws, so the contract a filter builder satisfies is strict.

nodes.label: #@ Note (tier/verb/family)
nodes.rationale: Values are case-sensitive because a program writes them; freehand text starts at the first token without '=' so malformed pairs are caught.

nodes.label: Extra Conditions as Ordinary Lines
nodes.rationale: No special marker for generated conditions: a marker would be a comment the game skips, so the validated filter would differ from the one that runs. Provenance goes in a trailing comment.

nodes.norm_label: gem buckets dominate the block count

nodes.label: One EC2 instance, many Elastic IPs
nodes.norm_label: one ec2 instance, many elastic ips
nodes.rationale: EIPs cost the same on any instance, so minimise compute; t4g.small holds 12 slots so scaling is allocating EIPs.

nodes.label: Open question: per-IP vs per-account limits
nodes.norm_label: open question: per-ip vs per-account limits

nodes.norm_label: open question: prefix or asn bucketing

nodes.label: Source-IP socket binding via secondary private IPs
nodes.norm_label: source-ip socket binding via secondary private ips
nodes.rationale: AWS 1:1 NATs each secondary private IP to its EIP; Amazon Linux 2023 sets up per-ENI policy routing.

nodes.label: No NAT Gateway, public subnet
nodes.rationale: A NAT Gateway costs money and collapses all workers to one address.

nodes.label: Rejected: Lambda
nodes.rationale: No control over egress IP inside or outside a VPC.

nodes.label: Rejected: NAT Gateway with secondary IPs
nodes.norm_label: rejected: nat gateway with secondary ips

nodes.label: .s3/panel/ storage (state.json, agent-feedback)
nodes.rationale: The old list format loses value types on a round trip, so keyed state is stored as-is.

nodes.label: Not built: feedback into training, Node eval prediction
nodes.norm_label: not built: feedback into training, node eval prediction

nodes.label: extractFeatures
nodes.rationale: Extract generously: only extracted features can be discovered.

nodes.label: normalizeMod
nodes.rationale: Strip rolled numbers so one mod is one feature; prefer canonical stat ids when available.

nodes.label: S3 storage as batched gzipped NDJSON
nodes.norm_label: s3 storage as batched gzipped ndjson
nodes.rationale: Too much data for EBS; batching cuts PUT count and compresses JSON 5-10x.

nodes.label: GGG Currency Exchange history endpoint (web.poecdn.com/api/currency-exchange)
nodes.rationale: Public, hourly ids, all leagues in one payload, current hour never available, old entries may be pruned.

nodes.label: Ratio direction trap
nodes.rationale: Pair order is arbitrary hash order; compute both endpoints then min/max.

nodes.label: Storage grain: one row per (hour, league, market_id)
nodes.norm_label: storage grain: one row per (hour, league, market_id)
nodes.rationale: Store all leagues and filter at query time; derived stats are computed columns.

nodes.label: Link-finding pipeline (extract, count, prune, pair, score, view)
nodes.norm_label: link-finding pipeline (extract, count, prune, pair, score, view)
